findings.where: Style tile, the 'Type pair' row on desktop: the Source Sans 3 specimen in the right column
findings.fault: The type pair is split across the two columns. In every other row, the right column holds its own labelled section (Texture, Motion sketch). Here it holds an unlabelled Source Sans 3 specimen, so it looks like a separate block with a missing label rather than the second half of the pair. The two specimens also sit on different baselines and at very different sizes, so they don't read as one row. Proximity groups the serif with its own paragraph and leaves the sans on its own.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, reading the tile to rule on the type pair. The two faces should be judged together, but the layout presents them as unrelated pieces.

findings.where: Style tile section labels, desktop and phone: 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' have a hairline rule under the label, but 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' do not
findings.fault: Labels of the same kind are treated two ways, which breaks similarity. On desktop the rule seems to depend on which column a section is in. On phone, where everything is one column, the rules come and go between sections for no visible reason, so the section rhythm looks uneven.
findings.who_objects: Whoever builds the layout round from this tile, and Angélique adding sections later. Neither can tell whether the ruled label is a rule of the look or an accident, so the inconsistency would be copied onto the site.

findings.where: Phone hero: the portrait stand-in below the 'Get in touch' button
findings.fault: At 390 px the portrait drops below the button and starts about 109 px in from the left. This leaves a narrow empty strip beside it that lines up with nothing above it. Instead of a figure running off the right edge, it reads as a block that slipped out of position. It is also cut off from the headline it should sit beside.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank visitor on a phone, for whom Mark should be the figure next to his words. They see a stray offset box after the call to action, which weakens the 'the man himself' arrangement the direction depends on.
